title: Change of rings between quasi-coherent algebras: quasi-coherence and affine sections
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C$ be sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_Y$-modules are quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], let $\varphi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras, and let $\mathcal P$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose underlying $\mathcal O_Y$-module (through $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B$) is quasi-coherent. Let $\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$ be the change of rings along $\varphi$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the sheafification of the presheaf $W\mapsto\mathcal P(W)\otimes_{\mathcal B(W)}\mathcal C(W)$, a sheaf of $\mathcal C$-modules, and let $t_W:\mathcal P(W)\otimes_{\mathcal B(W)}\mathcal C(W)\to(\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C)(W)$ be the component of the sheafification map. Then the underlying $\mathcal O_Y$-module of $\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$ (through $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$) is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $W\subseteq Y$ the map $t_W$ is bijective.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma 01SB (morphisms-lemma-affine-equivalence-modules): 'quasi-coherence is preserved by pullbacks and change of rings' (statement assembled by the agent); the affine computation is that of Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (schemes-lemma-widetilde-constructions, item (1)) and Section 01LA (schemes-section-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: Set-up: the change of rings is the $\mathcal O_Y$-module sheafification. Write $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_Y$; $\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ is the structure map, $\mathcal O\to\mathcal C$ is $\varphi$ composed with it, and every $\mathcal P(U)$ is an $\mathcal O(U)$-module through $\mathcal O(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$, $\mathcal C(U)$ a $\mathcal B(U)$-module through $\varphi_U$. Let $\mathcal T_p$ be the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal P(U)\otimes_{\mathcal B(U)}\mathcal C(U)$ of $\mathcal C$-modules (action on the right factor; restrictions induced by those of $\mathcal P$, $\mathcal B$, $\mathcal C$), $\mathcal T=\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C=\mathcal T_p^\#$ its sheafification as a presheaf of $\mathcal C$-modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $\eta:\mathcal T_p\to\mathcal T$ the sheafification map, so $t_W=\eta_W$. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (for the ring $\mathcal C$), the underlying sheaf of abelian groups of $\mathcal T$ is the sheafification of $\mathcal T_p$ as a presheaf of abelian groups, with $\eta$ its sheafification map; by the same definition for the ring $\mathcal O$, the $\mathcal O$-module sheafification of $\mathcal T_p$ (restricted to $\mathcal O$) is this same abelian sheaf with the unique map of sheaves of sets $\mathcal O\times\mathcal T\to\mathcal T$ extending the $\mathcal O$-action on $\mathcal T_p$. The action of $\mathcal O$ on $\mathcal T$ through $\mathcal O\to\mathcal C$ is such an extension, so the two agree: the underlying $\mathcal O$-module of $\mathcal T$, with $\eta$, is the $\mathcal O$-module sheafification of $\mathcal T_p$, and every $\mathcal O$-linear map from $\mathcal T_p$ to a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules factors uniquely through $\eta$ by an $\mathcal O$-linear map.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 0089 (sheaves-lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules) and the change of rings of Section sheaves-section-sheafification-presheaves-modules

proof.text: The tensor product over $\mathcal O$ and its two $\mathcal B$-actions. Let $\mathcal S=\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal C$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the $\mathcal O$-module sheafification of $\mathcal S_p:U\mapsto\mathcal P(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal C(U)$, with sheafification map $t^{\mathcal S}$. Since $\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal C$ are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O$-modules, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] gives: $\mathcal S$ is quasi-coherent and $t^{\mathcal S}_W$ is bijective for every affine open $W$. The presheaf $\mathcal S_p$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules in two ways: $b\cdot_1(p\otimes c)=bp\otimes c$ and $b\cdot_2(p\otimes c)=p\otimes\varphi(b)c$ (well defined because $(b,p,c)\mapsto bp\otimes c$ and $(b,p,c)\mapsto p\otimes\varphi(b)c$ are $\mathcal O(U)$-balanced in $(p,c)$, $\mathcal O(U)$ acting on $\mathcal P(U)$ and $\mathcal C(U)$ through $\mathcal B(U)$ and $\varphi_U$, which is a map of $\mathcal O(U)$-algebras; both commute with restrictions); restricted along $\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ each gives back the $\mathcal O$-module structure of $\mathcal S_p$. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (for the ring $\mathcal B$) the $\mathcal B$-module sheafification of $(\mathcal S_p,\cdot_i)$ is the abelian sheafification $\mathcal S$ with an action $\cdot_i$ of $\mathcal B$ for which $t^{\mathcal S}$ is $\mathcal B$-linear; restricted along $\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ it extends the $\mathcal O$-action of $\mathcal S_p$, so by the uniqueness in the same definition it is the $\mathcal O$-module structure of $\mathcal S$. Moreover for every sheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules $\mathcal H$ and $\mathcal B$-linear $g:(\mathcal S_p,\cdot_i)\to\mathcal H$, the unique $\mathcal O$-linear $\bar g:\mathcal S\to\mathcal H$ with $\bar g\circ t^{\mathcal S}=g$ is $\mathcal B$-linear for $\cdot_i$ (the $\mathcal B$-linear factorization exists and is $\mathcal O$-linear, hence equals $\bar g$).

source.place: Modules, Section 01CA (modules-section-tensor-product); Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (schemes-lemma-widetilde-constructions) item (1) and Section 01LA, through the cited node

proof.text: The relation map. Let $\mathcal F=\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal S$ with sheafification map $t^{\mathcal F}$; $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal S$ (Step 2) are quasi-coherent, so by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and $t^{\mathcal F}_W:\mathcal B(W)\otimes_{\mathcal O(W)}\mathcal S(W)\to\mathcal F(W)$ is bijective for affine $W$. For $i=1,2$ the maps $\mathcal B(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal S(U)\to\mathcal S(U)$, $b\otimes s\mapsto b\cdot_is$, are well defined ($\cdot_i$ restricts to the $\mathcal O$-structure, Step 2), $\mathcal O(U)$-linear and compatible with restrictions; by the universal property of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] they induce $\mathcal O$-linear $a_i:\mathcal F\to\mathcal S$ with $a_i(t^{\mathcal F}(b\otimes s))=b\cdot_is$. Put $\delta=a_1-a_2:\mathcal F\to\mathcal S$, a morphism of $\mathcal O$-modules between quasi-coherent $\mathcal O$-modules.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma 01SB (morphisms-lemma-affine-equivalence-modules): 'quasi-coherence is preserved by ... change of rings' (argument written by the agent)

proof.text: The cokernel. Let $q:\mathcal S\to\mathcal T'=\operatorname{Coker}\delta$ be the cokernel of $\delta$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (2), (3): $\mathcal T'$ is quasi-coherent, $q$ is an epimorphism with $q\circ\delta=0$, and for every affine open $W$ the map $q_W:\mathcal S(W)\to\mathcal T'(W)$ is surjective with kernel $\delta_W(\mathcal F(W))$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IB (schemes-lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent) and Section 01LA (schemes-section-quasi-coherent), through the cited node

proof.text: Sections of $\mathcal T'$ over an affine open. Algebra fact (used for any open $U$): for a ring map $R\to B_0$, a $B_0$-module $P_0$ and a $B_0$-algebra $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$, the map $\pi:P_0\otimes_RC_0\to P_0\otimes_{B_0}C_0$, $p\otimes c\mapsto p\otimes c$, is surjective with kernel the $R$-submodule $N$ spanned by $b\cdot_1x-b\cdot_2x$ ($b\in B_0$, $x\in P_0\otimes_RC_0$), equivalently by $bp\otimes c-p\otimes\varphi_0(b)c$. Indeed $\pi$ kills $N$; and $(p,c)\mapsto$ class of $p\otimes c$ in $(P_0\otimes_RC_0)/N$ is biadditive and $B_0$-balanced (its $R$-balancedness is part of this since $R$ acts through $B_0$), so it induces $P_0\otimes_{B_0}C_0\to(P_0\otimes_RC_0)/N$, inverse to the map induced by $\pi$ on generators. Now let $W$ be affine, $R=\mathcal O(W)$, $B_0=\mathcal B(W)$, $C_0=\mathcal C(W)$, $P_0=\mathcal P(W)$. Every element of $\mathcal F(W)$ is $t^{\mathcal F}_W(\sum_kb_k\otimes s_k)$ and every $s_k=t^{\mathcal S}_W(x_k)$ (Steps 2, 3), so, as $t^{\mathcal S}$ is $\mathcal B$-linear for $\cdot_1,\cdot_2$ (Step 2), $\delta_W(\mathcal F(W))=\{\sum_k t^{\mathcal S}_W(b_k\cdot_1x_k-b_k\cdot_2x_k)\}=t^{\mathcal S}_W(N)$. By Step 4 and the algebra fact, $q_W\circ t^{\mathcal S}_W$ induces a bijection $\lambda_W:P_0\otimes_{B_0}C_0\to\mathcal T'(W)$, $p\otimes c\mapsto q_W(t^{\mathcal S}_W(p\otimes c))$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (schemes-lemma-widetilde-constructions); the algebra fact is the presentation of a tensor product over B_0 as a quotient of the one over R (written out by the agent)

proof.text: Comparison maps. (a) $\rho:\mathcal T\to\mathcal T'$. For every open $U$ the map $\mathcal S_p(U)\to\mathcal T'(U)$, $x\mapsto q_U(t^{\mathcal S}_U(x))$, kills $b\cdot_1x-b\cdot_2x$, because $t^{\mathcal S}(b\cdot_1x-b\cdot_2x)=b\cdot_1t^{\mathcal S}(x)-b\cdot_2t^{\mathcal S}(x)=\delta(t^{\mathcal F}(b\otimes t^{\mathcal S}(x)))$ (Steps 2, 3) and $q\circ\delta=0$ (Step 4); by the algebra fact of Step 5 it factors through $\pi_U:\mathcal S_p(U)\to\mathcal T_p(U)$, giving an $\mathcal O(U)$-linear map compatible with restrictions, $p\otimes c\mapsto q_U(t^{\mathcal S}_U(p\otimes c))$. By Step 1 there is a unique $\mathcal O$-linear $\rho$ with $\rho\circ\eta\circ\pi=q\circ t^{\mathcal S}$. (b) $\sigma:\mathcal S\to\mathcal T$. The map $\eta\circ\pi:\mathcal S_p\to\mathcal T$ is $\mathcal O$-linear and, for each $i$, $\mathcal B$-linear for $\cdot_i$, where $\mathcal T$ is a $\mathcal B$-module through $\varphi$ (in $\mathcal T_p(U)$, $bp\otimes c=p\otimes\varphi(b)c=b(p\otimes c)$). By Step 2 the induced $\mathcal O$-linear $\sigma:\mathcal S\to\mathcal T$ with $\sigma\circ t^{\mathcal S}=\eta\circ\pi$ is $\mathcal B$-linear for $\cdot_1$ and for $\cdot_2$. Hence $\sigma(\delta(t^{\mathcal F}(b\otimes s)))=\sigma(b\cdot_1s)-\sigma(b\cdot_2s)=b\sigma(s)-b\sigma(s)=0$, so $\sigma\circ\delta\circ t^{\mathcal F}=0$ and, by uniqueness in the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\sigma\circ\delta=0$. As $q$ is the cokernel of $\delta$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ (Step 4) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\sigma=\bar\sigma\circ q$ for a unique $\mathcal O$-linear $\bar\sigma:\mathcal T'\to\mathcal T$. (c) Inverse. $\rho\bar\sigma q\,t^{\mathcal S}=\rho\sigma t^{\mathcal S}=\rho\eta\pi=q\,t^{\mathcal S}$, so $\rho\bar\sigma q=q$ by uniqueness in the universal property of $t^{\mathcal S}$, and $\rho\bar\sigma=\mathrm{id}$ because $q$ is an epimorphism. $\bar\sigma\rho\eta\pi=\bar\sigma q\,t^{\mathcal S}=\sigma t^{\mathcal S}=\eta\pi$; each $\pi_U$ is surjective, so $\bar\sigma\rho\eta=\eta$ and $\bar\sigma\rho=\mathrm{id}$ by Step 1. So $\rho$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O$-modules.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 0089 (sheaves-lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property (argument written by the agent)

proof.text: Conclusion. $\mathcal T'$ is quasi-coherent (Step 4) and $\rho:\mathcal T\to\mathcal T'$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O$-modules (Step 6); if $\mathcal T'|_U\cong\widetilde M$ on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, then $\mathcal T|_U\cong\widetilde M$, so the underlying $\mathcal O_Y$-module of $\mathcal T=\mathcal P\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent]. For an affine open $W$, $\rho_W\circ t_W=\rho_W\circ\eta_W$ sends $p\otimes c$ to $q_W(t^{\mathcal S}_W(p\otimes c))$ (Step 6 (a)), i.e. $\rho_W\circ t_W=\lambda_W$, which is bijective (Step 5); as $\rho_W$ is bijective, so is $t_W$.
